title: Building on ServiceNow’s Latest AI: Practical Patterns for Now Assist, AI Control Tower, and Virtual Agent
excerpt: Learn how to apply the latest ServiceNow AI capabilities—including Now Assist v2.0 models, AI Control Tower, Virtual Agent AI, and AI Search—in real workflows. This guide focuses on concrete GlideRecord and Flow Designer patterns you can reuse in your own apps.
content:
Overview

ServiceNow’s AI stack has matured into a cohesive platform: updated Now Assist models, AI Control Tower, Predictive Intelligence, Virtual Agent AI, AI Search, and deep LLM integrations. Recent releases add higher-quality ServiceNow AI Models v2.0 for Now Assist, expanded Microsoft and third-party LLM integrations with governance, and new AI-powered experiences in workspace UIs.

For developers, the opportunity is to orchestrate these capabilities from server-side scripts and Flow Designer, so AI is embedded directly into records, tasks, and custom apps—not tacked on as a chatbot.

Implementation

Now Assist and ServiceNow AI Models v2.0

New instances and upgrades now default to ServiceNow AI Models v2.0 for Now Assist, improving summarization, action suggestions, and knowledge answers across workspaces.

A common pattern is to let Now Assist summarize large incident histories and save a concise summary on the record for reporting or handoffs.

// Example: Generate and persist an AI summary for an Incident
// Assumes you’ve configured Now Assist for ITSM and enabled summarization

var incidentGr = new GlideRecord('incident');
if (incidentGr.get(current.sys_id)) {
  // Build the prompt from comments/work notes
  var workNotes = '';
  var journalGr = new GlideRecord('sys_journal_field');
  journalGr.addQuery('element_id', current.sys_id);
  journalGr.addQuery('element', 'work_notes');
  journalGr.orderBy('sys_created_on');
  journalGr.query();
  while (journalGr.next()) {
    workNotes += '\n[' + journalGr.sys_created_on + '] ' + journalGr.value;
  }

  // Call a Scripted REST API or Script Include that wraps the GenAI Controller / Now Assist APIs
  var ai = new NowAssistUtils(); // your Script Include
  var summary = ai.summarizeIncident(incidentGr.number.toString(), workNotes);

  incidentGr.u_ai_summary = summary;
  incidentGr.update();
}

In this pattern, the Script Include encapsulates Now Assist / GenAI Controller calls, keeping your business logic clean.

AI Control Tower, Predictive Intelligence, and Flow Designer

AI Control Tower centralizes LLMs (ServiceNow models plus Microsoft/OpenAI/etc.), safety rules, and usage policies. Predictive Intelligence continues to drive auto-routing, categorization, and recommendations based on ML models trained on your data.

A typical developer workflow:

  1. Use Predictive Intelligence to auto-classify and route records.
  2. Use AI Control Tower to call a governed LLM for generative tasks (summaries, drafts, explanations).
  3. Orchestrate both via Flow Designer actions and subflows.
// Server-side helper: invoke an AI Control Tower endpoint via REST

var AiTowerClient = Class.create();
AiTowerClient.prototype = {
  initialize: function() {},

  generateResolutionSuggestion: function(incidentSysId) {
    var inc = new GlideRecord('incident');
    if (!inc.get(incidentSysId))
      return '';

    var r = new sn_ws.RESTMessageV2('x_your_app.ai_control_tower', 'generate_resolution');
    r.setRequestBody(JSON.stringify({
      short_description: inc.short_description.toString(),
      description: inc.description.toString(),
      category: inc.category.toString(),
      subcategory: inc.subcategory.toString()
    }));

    var res = r.execute();
    var body = res.getBody();
    var parsed = JSON.parse(body);
    return parsed.suggestion || '';
  },

  type: 'AiTowerClient'
};

In Flow Designer, expose this via an Action that takes an Incident Sys ID and writes the returned suggestion to a work note or custom field.

Virtual Agent AI, NLU, and MCP / Agent-to-Agent

Virtual Agent now uses generative AI to handle more open-ended questions, with improved NLU models. With Agent-to-Agent (A2A) and MCP-style protocols, you can let ServiceNow agents collaborate with external AI agents or tools while keeping the Virtual Agent conversation in control.

Typical integration pattern:

  • Virtual Agent topic collects user intent and context.
  • Flow Designer subflow calls an external tool or AI agent (via API, MCP, or other protocol).
  • Virtual Agent presents the AI agent’s result, with guardrails defined in AI Control Tower.
// Example: GlideRecord step in a Virtual Agent action to fetch user’s open requests

var gr = new GlideRecord('sc_request');
gr.addQuery('requested_for', gs.getUserID());
gr.addActiveQuery();
gr.orderByDesc('sys_created_on');
gr.setLimit(5);
gr.query();

var results = [];
while (gr.next()) {
  results.push({
    number: gr.number.toString(),
    short_description: gr.short_description.toString(),
    state: gr.state.getDisplayValue()
  });
}

// Pass 'results' back to Virtual Agent as an array to render in a carousel or list

LLM Integration Patterns and AI Search

ServiceNow now supports seamless integration with Microsoft AI services and other LLMs, coordinated through AI Control Tower. AI Search provides vector-based, relevance-tuned search across records and knowledge.

Common patterns:

  • AI Search widget/Global Search with AI-powered answer snippets.
  • Server-side retrieve-then-generate: query AI Search, then send top results to an LLM via AI Control Tower for a tailored answer.
// Pseudo-pattern: retrieve-then-generate using AI Search + LLM

var query = 'How do I reset my VPN token?';

// 1. AI Search (example, using a custom Scripted REST or API wrapper)
var aiSearch = new AiSearchUtils();
var docs = aiSearch.searchKnowledge(query, 5); // returns array of {number, short_description, text}

// 2. Compose context for LLM
var contextText = '';
docs.forEach(function(doc, idx) {
  contextText += '\n[' + (idx+1) + '] ' + doc.short_description + '\n' + doc.text + '\n';
});

// 3. Call AI Control Tower to generate a consolidated answer
var tower = new AiTowerClient();
var answer = tower.generateAnswerFromContext(query, contextText);

// 4. Persist or return the answer
current.u_ai_answer = answer;
current.update();

Best Practices

  • Centralize AI calls in Script Includes: Wrap Now Assist, AI Control Tower, and external LLM calls in Script Includes to keep flows, UI Actions, and Business Rules simple.
  • Use Flow Designer for orchestration: Trigger AI-processing subflows from lifecycle events (create/update/close) instead of one-off scripts in forms.
  • Start with narrow, high-value use cases: Summaries, resolution suggestions, and classification are safer first steps than full autonomous flows.
  • Leverage AI Control Tower policies: Define which tables, fields, and roles are allowed to send data to external LLMs; log and review usage.
  • Keep prompts and context minimal but rich: Provide only relevant fields and a small set of related records or knowledge articles to reduce hallucination and latency.
  • Design Virtual Agent topics with clear guardrails: Use intent detection and topic routing; fall back to classic scripted paths when confidence is low.
  • Monitor and retrain Predictive Intelligence models: Regularly review classification accuracy and retrain when data or routing logic changes.
  • Version your prompts: Store prompts and config in sys_properties or custom tables so you can iterate without code changes.

Common Pitfalls

  • Calling LLMs directly from many places: Scattering REST calls in Business Rules, Scripted REST APIs, and UI Actions leads to inconsistent behavior and policy bypass. Always route through a shared utility or AI Control Tower configuration.
  • Sending full records or logs to external models: Dumping entire incident histories or knowledge bases risks PII/PHI exposure and bloats tokens. Always filter to the minimal needed fields and anonymize where possible.
  • Skipping data hygiene before Predictive Intelligence: Training models on dirty or inconsistent data yields poor routing and recommendations. Clean your categories, assignment groups, and mandatory fields first.
  • Over-automating Virtual Agent: Letting generative responses handle every query without explicit intents, disambiguation, or exit paths frustrates users. Preserve deterministic flows for critical processes.
  • Ignoring observability: Not logging prompts, responses, and decisions from AI-powered flows makes debugging and compliance audits difficult. Capture AI activity (with redaction) in a dedicated log table or ATF tests.
  • Blocking human override: AI-suggested categories, resolutions, or summaries must be editable by agents. Avoid hard enforcement via Business Rules that reject human corrections.
  • Tight coupling to a single LLM provider: Hard-coding vendor-specific APIs undermines AI Control Tower’s value. Use its abstraction so you can switch providers without rewriting flows.

title: This Week’s ServiceNow Platform Updates: Yokohama/Xanadu, Impact Platform Health, and Employee Center
excerpt: This guide distills the latest ServiceNow platform updates from official docs and community posts into concrete actions for developers. Learn what’s new in Yokohama/Xanadu, Impact Platform Health, Employee Center, and how to safely upgrade, harden security, and improve performance with practical examples.
content:
Overview

The past week has brought a cluster of important ServiceNow updates across the core platform, Impact Platform Health, Employee Center, and Store apps. As a developer, these changes affect how you plan Yokohama/Xanadu upgrades, monitor platform health, and deliver better employee experiences.

This guide focuses on what you can act on now: how to prepare and test upgrades, wire the new Platform Health capabilities into your workflows, adopt Employee Center enhancements, and apply security and performance best practices from recent knowledge content.

Yokohama/Xanadu Release Features and Upgrade Guidance

ServiceNow continues to ship patches and hotfixes for the Yokohama family, with updated guidance in the official release notes and upgrade center.

Key themes for Yokohama/Xanadu

  • Ongoing patches and hotfixes – The Yokohama release notes list new patch levels and important fixes across platform, security, and performance.
  • App Version–aware upgrades – Recent Platform Academy content highlights strategies to upgrade with confidence using app versioning and consistent automation.
  • AI-first capabilities – The core platform continues to evolve as an AI control tower, so instances should be kept close to current families to leverage these capabilities.

Practical upgrade flow

  1. Inventory and freeze

    Identify in-progress development and freeze non-critical changes before requesting an upgrade in your sub‑prod instances.

    // Simple inventory of in-progress update sets
var us = new GlideRecord('sys_update_set');
us.addActiveQuery();
us.addQuery('state', 'in progress');
us.query();
while (us.next()) {
  gs.print(us.name + ' - ' + us.sys_id);
}
  2. Align app versions

    Use the application manager to confirm your scoped apps are on versions compatible with Yokohama/Xanadu before scheduling the family upgrade.

  3. Automate regression checks

    Register critical-path checks in ATF (Automated Test Framework) and run them as a gate before and after upgrading each environment.

    // Example: create an ATF test programmatically
var test = new GlideRecord('sys_atf_test');
test.initialize();
test.name = 'Critical Incident Flow – Post-Upgrade';
test.description = 'Validates core incident creation and assignment.';
test.active = true;
var testId = test.insert();
// Add steps via ATF APIs or UI as needed
  4. Promote with app version control

    Use a consistent promotion pattern (dev → test → prod) and avoid local hotfixes that diverge app versions by environment.

Anti‑patterns to avoid

  • Upgrading production before running ATF and sanity checks on a representative sub‑prod environment.
  • Skipping app version review and discovering incompatibilities only after the family upgrade.
  • Leaving long‑lived in‑progress update sets that span multiple family versions.

Platform Health and Impact Capabilities Updates

The December Store release introduces expanded ServiceNow Impact Platform Health capabilities, including real-time prevention, diagnostic scans, and improved dashboards for developers.

What’s new in Impact Platform Health

  • Real-Time Messaging & Prevention – Proactive alerts and preventive guidance when risky configurations or patterns are detected in near real time.
  • Automated Diagnostic Scans – Configurable scans that run nightly, weekly, or monthly to detect common issues across your instance landscape.
  • Developer-centric Dashboards – Each developer gets a personalized view of findings, exceptions, and technical debt to prioritize remediation.

Configuring scheduled diagnostic scans

Platform Health configuration lets admins define scan cadences per instance. You can also trigger scans or respond to findings with server-side logic.

// Example: post-scan handler to create tasks for high severity findings
var finding = new GlideRecord('sn_impact_ph_finding');
finding.addQuery('severity', 'high');
finding.addQuery('state', 'new');
finding.query();
while (finding.next()) {
  var task = new GlideRecord('sn_custom_tech_debt');
  task.initialize();
  task.short_description = 'Platform Health finding: ' + finding.name;
  task.description = finding.description;
  task.priority = 1; // Critical
  task.u_finding = finding.sys_id;
  task.insert();

  finding.state = 'task_created';
  finding.update();
}

Best practices for Platform Health adoption

  • Start with weekly scans in non‑prod to tune noise, then enable nightly scans in production.
  • Treat findings as work items: route to the right teams, track SLAs, and close the loop with root-cause fixes.
  • Use developer dashboards in sprint planning to prioritize high-impact debt over low‑value cosmetic fixes.

Common Platform Health anti‑patterns

  • Running scans but not integrating findings into any work intake process (they quickly become ignored noise).
  • Disabling rules that generate findings instead of remediating underlying issues.
  • Scanning only production while ignoring technical debt accumulating in dev/test.

Store App Releases and Employee Center Enhancements

The December 2025 Store release also delivers new features across ServiceNow Impact and Employee Center (Pro).

Employee Center (Pro) December enhancements

Recent enhancements focus on improving discoverability, content targeting, and experience configuration.

  • Richer Employee Center layouts – New layout options and page components make it easier to compose branded, task-focused employee hubs.
  • Improved content targeting – Finer-grained criteria for who sees which content, driven by user attributes and contextual signals.
  • Better search and topic experience – Updated search components and topic pages to surface relevant knowledge and services more quickly.

Practical configuration example

// Example: Assign a topic page to a specific user criteria
var crit = new GlideRecord('sn_ec_user_criteria');
crit.addQuery('name', 'Canada Employees');
crit.query();
if (crit.next()) {
  var topic = new GlideRecord('sn_ec_topic_page');
  topic.addQuery('title', 'Benefits & Leave');
  topic.query();
  if (topic.next()) {
    var map = new GlideRecord('sn_ec_topic_user_criteria_m2m');
    map.initialize();
    map.topic_page = topic.sys_id;
    map.user_criteria = crit.sys_id;
    map.insert();
  }
}

Impact Store updates you should care about

  • New Platform Health experiences – The December Impact Store release bundles the Platform Health improvements described above.
  • Store delivery model – Many Impact capabilities are delivered via the Store, so staying current with Store app versions is as important as family upgrades.

Security Patches and Performance Improvements

The Yokohama release notes and available patches pages highlight ongoing security and performance fixes for the family.

Actionable security steps

  • Track the latest Yokohama patches and apply them to non-prod quickly, promoting to prod after validation.
  • Enable and monitor security-related system properties recommended by release notes (for example, stricter default ACL behavior or encryption options where available).
  • Use Impact Platform Health to surface insecure patterns, such as global ACLs or direct table writes from client scripts.
// Example: quick scan for overly permissive ACLs
var acl = new GlideRecord('sys_security_acl');
acl.addQuery('type', 'record');
acl.addNullQuery('condition');
acl.addNullQuery('script');
acl.query();
while (acl.next()) {
  gs.print('ACL without condition/script: ' + acl.name + ' on ' + acl.operation);
}

Performance tuning themes

  • Apply hotfixes aimed at query performance and caching issues listed in the Yokohama patches page.
  • Use Performance Analytics, Platform Health, and logs to find slow transactions and long-running scripts.
  • Refactor synchronous work into background or asynchronous flows where latency is not user‑critical.

Best Practices from Recent Knowledge and Community Content

Recent Knowledge Base and community posts emphasize predictable upgrades, AI‑ready architectures, and disciplined configuration practices.

Key best practices

  • Design for AI-first features – Use standard data models, consistent task types, and well-defined APIs so generative and agentic AI features can reason over your workflows.
  • Favor configuration over customization – Use out-of-the-box flows, UI components, and patterns first; only customize where there is clear, quantified value.
  • Treat Store app versions as first-class – Establish a cadence to review and update Store apps (Impact, Employee Center, etc.) alongside family upgrades.
  • Automate guardrails – Capture guardrails (naming, ACL rules, integration patterns) as code and checks, not tribal knowledge.
// Guardrail example: prevent creation of client scripts on core tables via business rule
if (current.table == 'incident') {
  gs.addErrorMessage('Client scripts on incident are restricted. Use UI Policies or UX Components.');
  current.setAbortAction(true);
}

Common anti‑patterns highlighted in knowledge content

  • Running upgrades and Store app updates without documented rollback and test plans.
  • Using Employee Center as a static portal instead of an actively curated, data-driven experience.
  • Ignoring Impact Platform Health findings because "prod is working" until a critical incident occurs.
  • Embedding business logic directly in UI actions and client scripts instead of reusable Script Includes and APIs.

By combining the latest Yokohama/Xanadu patches, December Store updates, and Impact Platform Health capabilities, you can keep your instance secure, performant, and ready for the next wave of AI-driven features—without sacrificing stability.

title: Latest Enterprise AI and GenAI Breakthroughs: Accelerating Business Automation in ServiceNow
excerpt: This week brings major advancements in enterprise AI from Dell-NVIDIA integrations, Microsoft agentic AI tools, and adoption reports highlighting Copilot's dominance. ServiceNow developers can leverage these for smarter automation, from AI factories to LLM orchestration.
content:
Enterprise AI Shifts to Agentic Automation

Enterprise AI is rapidly evolving from pilots to production-scale deployments, with a strong focus on GenAI, LLMs, and AI agents for business automation. Recent announcements emphasize integrated platforms that streamline AI workloads, addressing key hurdles like data privacy, strategy gaps, and deployment complexity.

Dell and NVIDIA Advance AI Factories for Scalable Workloads

Dell Technologies' latest collaboration with NVIDIA introduces enhancements to the Dell AI Factory, including ObjectScale and PowerScale storage engines integrated with NVIDIA Dynamo. These accelerate AI application workflows and high-performance computing.

  • Automate AI model provisioning via PowerShell or REST APIs in Flow Designer.
  • Use NVIDIA-enabled servers for on-premises LLM inference in ServiceNow's Predictive Intelligence.
  • Deploy agentic workflows that trigger Dell ObjectScale for data-intensive automations.

Microsoft Copilot Leads Adoption Amid Privacy Challenges

Surveys show Microsoft Copilot adopted by 67.4% of enterprises, outpacing ChatGPT, due to its seamless Microsoft 365 integration. However, 54% of firms remain in pilot mode due to privacy concerns.

  • Embed Copilot outputs into Knowledge Management via Vancouver or Xanadu releases.
  • Build agentic flows using IntegrationHub to fetch Copilot-generated insights for ticket routing.
  • Address privacy by configuring on-premises LLMs with ServiceNow's Private AI capabilities.

Actionable Steps for ServiceNow Developers

  • Update Strategies: Adopt a platform-centric approach; assess Copilot integration via ServiceNow Store apps.
  • Build Agentic AI: Use Microsoft Ignite 2025 tools in Scripted REST APIs for multi-step automations.
  • Scale Securely: Pilot Dell/HPE factories with ServiceNow's Hyperautomation Hub.

title: Enterprise Automation, ITSM, and Digital Transformation: Practical Trends for ServiceNow Developers
excerpt: Enterprise automation is converging around AI-driven hyperautomation, low-code platforms, and data-first integration. This article gives ServiceNow developers actionable patterns, priorities, and implementation steps to apply these trends in real projects.
content:
What's Changing and Why It Matters

Enterprise automation is maturing from isolated RPA and scripted workflows into AI-driven hyperautomation combined with low-code/no-code tooling and stronger orchestration.

Top Trends ServiceNow Developers Should Prioritize

  • AI-native workflows and recommendations — Embed AI for classification, routing, and next-best-action within flows.
  • Hyperautomation & orchestration — Combine multiple automation types into orchestrated end-to-end processes.
  • Low-code/No-code enablement — Provide reusable Flow Designer actions and scoped apps.
  • Data-first integration — Treat integrations as data pipelines with normalized telemetry.
  • Automation governance and observability — Implement change controls and observability dashboards.

Concrete Implementation Patterns

  • AI-assisted triage pattern — Use a supervised ML model to pre-fill categorization and suggest routing.
  • Orchestrated end-to-end runbook — Create a Flow Designer flow that triggers on an event and calls external APIs.
  • Telemetry-driven remediation — Stream monitoring events into ServiceNow Event Management.

Developer Checklist Before Deployment

  • Define clear input/output contracts for every action.
  • Include comprehensive logging, idempotency, and dead-letter handling.
  • Automate tests that run in CI pipelines.
  • Apply least-privilege credentials for integrations.

title: New Integration Patterns, Flow Designer Tips, and Integration Hub Updates for ServiceNow Developers
excerpt: Practical guidance on current ServiceNow integration patterns, actionable Flow Designer tips, and recent Integration Hub capabilities to accelerate reliable, maintainable integrations.
content:
Overview — What's Changed and Why It Matters

ServiceNow integration patterns continue to converge on three goals: make integrations more resilient at scale, reduce custom code, and enable real-time or near-real-time data flows via streaming where appropriate.

Updated Integration Patterns to Use

  • API-first flow (REST/Scripted REST) for synchronous interactions: Use when a synchronous response is required.
  • Event/Stream-based for high-volume or low-latency needs: Use Stream Connect or message producers for telemetry.
  • ETL/Batch for bulk data and CMDB population: Use Integration Hub ETL actions for large imports.
  • Process API + Orchestration for cross-system workflows: Create lightweight process APIs that encapsulate business rules.

Practical Flow Designer Tips

  • Prefer subflows and reusable flow actions: Encapsulate repeated logic into subflows or custom actions.
  • Implement defensive error handling: Add retry policies, exponential backoff, and compensating flows.
  • Leverage dynamic inputs/outputs: Use introspection-capable actions to reduce maintenance.
  • Test with both unit and integration scenarios: Create mock REST endpoints and automate flow tests.

Integration Hub Updates

  • Starter Package: Basic SOAP/REST steps, JDBC, PowerShell, SFTP/SSH.
  • Professional Package: Advanced features like introspection for dynamic data handling.

title: Latest Trends in Enterprise Automation, ITSM, and Digital Transformation: Actionable Insights

title: Mastering ServiceNow Integrations in 2025: New Patterns, Flow Designer Tips, and Integration Hub Updates
excerpt: Discover the latest ServiceNow integration patterns with the updated Decision Tree, essential Flow Designer tips for efficient automation, and key Integration Hub enhancements like 200+ new connectors.
content:
New ServiceNow Integration Patterns for 2025

ServiceNow's Integration Pattern Decision Tree, updated to version 3.1 in September 2025, provides a flowchart to select the optimal pattern for third-party connections.

  • Real-time pull: Use SubFlow with Integration Hub for synchronous responses via Scripted REST API.
  • Scheduled imports: Leverage Integration Hub ETL, Process API, or Table API for CMDB data.
  • High-volume streaming: Opt for Flow Action Kafka Producer step or Scriptable ProducerV2 API in Stream Connect.

Flow Designer Tips for Developers

Flow Designer simplifies no-code/low-code automation, especially with Integration Hub. Key tips include:

  • Combine REST/SOAP steps with Payload Builder, Retry Policies, and Remote Tables for robust flows.
  • Implement error handling in Data Stream actions with Stream Connect alerts from the Yokohama release.
  • For custom needs, build Integration Hub-compatible spokes or use professional packages.

Integration Hub Updates and Expansion

Integration Hub now boasts over 200 pre-built connectors, enabling thousands of quick setups without custom code.

  • Starter Package: Basic SOAP/REST steps, JDBC, PowerShell, SFTP/SSH.
  • Professional Package: Advanced features like introspection for dynamic data handling.

title: This Week in Enterprise AI: GenAI, LLMs, and Agents — Practical Takeaways for ServiceNow Developers
excerpt: Major vendors released model and agent updates this week that push multimodal reasoning, cheaper inference, and agent-first integrations. ServiceNow developers should focus on connectors, orchestration, security, and observability.
content:
Key Developments and What They Mean

This week saw coordinated advances from major AI vendors emphasizing multimodal LLMs, lower-cost inference, and agentic capabilities that are moving autonomous workflows from experiments into production.

  • Multimodal, higher-reasoning models are now mainstream — Vendors announced new multimodal releases with improved reasoning and coding skills.
  • Agent-first features accelerate automation — Agent capabilities (long-horizon planning, tool use, parallel thought streams) are being prioritized.
  • Costs and performance improve — Recent launches include lower-priced model variants and faster inference tiers.

Top Practical Actions for ServiceNow Projects

  • Design agent interfaces, not just prompts — Define a clear agent contract: input context, allowed tools, retry/timeout policies.
  • Build robust connectors and adapters — Prioritize lightweight, auditable adapters to target internal systems.
  • Implement observation and tracing — Add request/response tracing and action logs to ServiceNow workflows.
  • Embed safety and least-privilege in agents — Give agents scoped, tokenized credentials and enforce RBAC policies.

Patterns and Architectures to Adopt

  • Hybrid orchestration layer — Place an orchestration service between ServiceNow and model endpoints.
  • Agent capability registry — Maintain a registry of available agent tools with metadata.
  • Human-in-the-loop checkpoints — Design human approval steps for actions with material impact.

title: 2025 Trends in Enterprise Automation, ITSM, and Digital Transformation: A ServiceNow Developer's Guide
excerpt: Explore the latest 2025 trends in enterprise automation, ITSM, and digital transformation, including hyperautomation, AI integration, and low-code platforms. Discover actionable insights tailored for platform customization.
content:
Introduction to 2025 Enterprise Trends

Enterprise automation in 2025 is dominated by hyperautomation, AI-driven processes, and low-code platforms, fundamentally reshaping ITSM and digital transformation. These trends enable end-to-end automation of business processes, reducing costs by up to 30% and enhancing scalability.

Hyperautomation: The Core of Enterprise Efficiency

Hyperautomation, coined by Gartner, combines RPA, AI, machine learning, and process mining to automate interconnected tasks across organizations. In ITSM, this means automating ticket resolution, service requests, and compliance checks seamlessly.

By 2025, hyperautomation optimizes finance, customer service, and logistics, with cloud trends like Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) and DevOps CI/CD pipelines accelerating deployments. ServiceNow's IT Operations Management (ITOM) module supports IaC for Visibility and Service Mapping.

AI and ML: Intelligent ITSM Workflows

AI integration is central, with NLP platforms automating customer interactions and ML for anomaly detection. In ServiceNow, Virtual Agent and Predictive Intelligence use ML to forecast incidents and auto-resolve issues.

Low-Code/No-Code: Democratizing Automation

No-code platforms empower non-developers, but ServiceNow's App Engine and Creator Workflows take this further for enterprise ITSM. Build custom apps without deep coding, automating approvals and change management.

ITSM-Specific Impacts and ServiceNow Strategies

  • Implement hyperautomation: Use Orchestration and RPA Hub to chain workflows.
  • AI for predictions: Train models in Studio for incident prioritization.
  • Low-code ITSM apps: Rapidly prototype with Studio, deploy via Store.
  • Security focus: Automate vulnerability response with SecOps.

title: Building AI Agents in ServiceNow: A Complete Guide

content:
Introduction

What are AI Agents?

AI Agents are autonomous systems that can perceive their environment, make decisions, and take actions to achieve specific goals. In ServiceNow, these agents can handle everything from incident resolution to complex approval workflows.

Getting Started

title: Flow Designer Best Practices for Enterprise Scale
excerpt: Essential patterns and anti-patterns when building flows that need to handle thousands of executions daily.
content:
Why Flow Designer Matters

Flow Designer is ServiceNow's powerful low-code automation tool. But with great power comes great responsibility—especially at enterprise scale.

Best Practices

  • Use Subflows: Break complex logic into reusable subflows
  • Error Handling: Always implement try-catch patterns
  • Async Operations: Use async for heavy processing
  • Monitoring: Track execution times and failures

Anti-Patterns to Avoid

Don't create flows that query large datasets without filters. Always use indexed fields and limit result sets.

// Bad: Queries all incidents
var gr = new GlideRecord('incident');
gr.query();

// Good: Filtered query
var gr = new GlideRecord('incident');
gr.addQuery('state', 1);
gr.addQuery('sys_created_on', '>=', gs.daysAgo(7));
gr.setLimit(100);
gr.query();

title: The Future of Enterprise AI: 2025 Trends

Enterprise AI in 2025

The enterprise AI landscape is evolving at an unprecedented pace. Here are the key trends shaping the industry this year.

Trend 1: Agentic AI

The shift from simple automation to intelligent agents that can reason, plan, and execute complex tasks autonomously. These agents don't just follow rules—they adapt to situations.
